crossRefs.note: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
For you write bitter things against me, and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth:
But now you count my steps. Don’t you watch over my sin?
Isn’t your wickedness great? Neither is there any end to your iniquities.
if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.
He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.
Yahweh God of Armies, how long will you be angry against the prayer of your people?
You are Yahweh, even you alone. You have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their army, the earth and all…
Your righteousness is like the mountains of God. Your judgments are like a great deep. Yahweh, you preserve man and…
Am I a sea, or a sea monster, that you put a guard over me?
For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in…
I was at ease, and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also set me up…
For you will make them turn their back, when you aim drawn bows at their face.
He has bent his bow, and set me as a mark for the arrow.
“Therefore I will not keep silent. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit. I will complain in the bitterness of my…
For my sighing comes before I eat. My groanings are poured out like water.

translations.web: If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you set me as a mark for you, so that I am a burden to myself?
translations.bsb: If I have sinned, what have I done to You, O watcher of mankind? Why have You made me Your target, so that I am a burden to You ?
translations.kjv: I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden
translations.asv: If I have sinned, what do I unto thee, O thou watcher of men? Why hast thou set me as a mark for thee, So that I am a burden to myself?
